# Tungsten PFC {#sec-tungsten}

`apps/tungsten` — the production phase-field crystal application, and the model
behind the scalability measurements in @sec-scalability.

## Physical setting

Phase-field crystal describes a crystalline solid through a continuous,
periodic density field $\psi(\mathbf{x},t)$ whose minima sit on lattice sites.
Because the field is continuous but its ground state is periodic, PFC resolves
elasticity, defects, and grain boundaries on diffusive time scales rather than
the vibrational scales molecular dynamics is bound to. This application is
parameterised for tungsten and is used for solidification and defect studies in
three dimensions.

The physical question the shipped configurations pose is a solidification one:
**place one or more crystalline nuclei in an undercooled melt and watch the
solid grow — where does the front sit, how fast does it advance, and what
happens where two differently oriented grains meet?** The observable the
application actually records is the **tracked solidification-front position**
along $x$ (the `moving` boundary's `xpos`, checkpointed and restartable),
together with the conserved global density and the field checksums that pin the
run. Grain structure is available as field output but is not reduced to a
number by this application.

## Problem setup

Six JSON presets ship (with matching TOML twins). They are all demonstration or
performance configurations: **none of them is executed by the test suite**,
which builds equivalent configurations in C++ instead. The table describes
`tungsten_moving_bc.json`, the directional-solidification case, and
`tungsten_single_seed.json`, the smallest one.

| Item | Directional solidification (`tungsten_moving_bc.json`) | Single seed (`tungsten_single_seed.json`) |
|---|---|---|
| Use case | A solidification front sweeping through undercooled tungsten, with a grid of differently oriented seeds ahead of it | The smallest runnable case: one BCC nucleus in a melt |
| Domain | $128 \times 64 \times 64$ cells at $\Delta x = 2\pi/(4\sqrt2) \approx 1.1107$, i.e. $142.2 \times 71.1 \times 71.1$ in reduced PFC length units, origin at the corner | $32^3$ cells at the same spacing, i.e. $35.5^3$, origin at the centre |
| Grid | Eight cells per BCC lattice constant ($a = 2\pi\sqrt2$ when the correlation peak sits at $\lvert\mathbf{k}\rvert = 1$); $t \in [0, 20000]$ at $\Delta t = 1$, output every 100 | Same spacing; $t \in [0, 10]$ at $\Delta t = 1$, output every step |
| Boundary conditions | Periodic on all three axes — see below — plus a `moving` density-reservoir band of width 15 that tracks the front and stays 40 units ahead of it | Periodic on all three axes plus a stationary `fixed` reservoir band |
| Initial condition | Uniform $\psi = -0.10$, then `seed_grid`: a $2 \times 2$ array of BCC seeds of radius 25 at $x = 30$, each jittered in position by $\pm 0.2 R$ and given a random orientation from a fixed RNG seed (42), so the run is deterministic | Uniform $\psi = -0.4$, then `single_seed`: one BCC nucleus built from the six $\{110\}$ wave vectors, amplitude $0.215936$, $\rho_{\mathrm{seed}} = -0.047$ |
| Key physical parameters | $T = 3300$, $T_0 = 156000$ (the TOML comments label both **kelvin**; only the ratio $T/T_0$ ever enters, through $e^{-T/T_0}$); coexistence densities $n_{\mathrm{sol}} = -0.047$, $n_{\mathrm{vap}} = -0.464$; peak amplitude $B_x = 0.8582$, width $\alpha = 0.5$; polynomial coefficients $p_2,p_3,p_4$ and $q_{20},\dots,q_{40}$. Lengths and times are **reduced PFC units** — the repository contains no conversion to nanometres or seconds | Identical parameter block |
| Observable | Tracked front position $x_{\mathrm{pos}}$ (checkpointed); `SPECTRAL_CHECKSUM` sum, sum of squares and $L^2$ of $\psi$; binary field dumps | Same checksums; $\psi$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{MF}}$ dumps |
| Model maturity | numerical verification: **regression** — split-run equivalence to $10^{-12}$, one pinned CPU checksum, CPU/GPU parity; the analytical checks that exist cover the ETD coefficients, not the model · physical completeness: **extended** — a fitted multi-term equation of state with a vapour branch and a mean-field-filtered density, beyond the canonical single-peak PFC · calibration: **representative**, with a caveat: the coefficients are described as a tungsten parameterisation, but **no source is cited anywhere in this repository** for $B_x$, $T_0$, $n_{\mathrm{sol}}$, $n_{\mathrm{vap}}$ or the polynomial coefficients, so they cannot be traced from it | Same |

Two things about this setup are easy to misread.

**"Fixed" and "moving" are not boundary conditions in the usual sense.** The
FFT treats the domain as periodic on all three axes, always; there is no
non-periodic path. What `fixed` and `moving` do is overlay a sigmoid density
band near one end of the box every step, pulling $\psi$ towards
$\rho_{\mathrm{low}}$ outside the band and $\rho_{\mathrm{high}}$ inside it.
Physically that band is a reservoir that keeps a melt region available for the
front to grow into and stops the growing solid from meeting its own periodic
image head-on. It is a penalty layer inside a periodic box, not a wall. What it
excludes is a real free surface: there is no vapour interface, no substrate,
and no container.

**The single-seed preset does not show a seed.** `SingleSeed` hard-codes its
radius at 64 reduced units, which is larger than the $17.8$-unit half-width of
the $32^3$ box, so the "seed" fills the entire domain and no melt is left
around it. That preset is a runnable smoke configuration, not a nucleation
experiment; the smallest shipped configuration that actually shows a nucleus in
melt is the $256^3$ `tungsten_single_seed_256_cuda.json`.

## Governing equations

The dynamics are conserved,

$$
\partial_t \psi \;=\; \nabla^2 \frac{\delta F}{\delta \psi},
$$ {#eq-w-dyn}

so the spatial mean of $\psi$ is a constant of the motion. The free energy
splits into a quadratic part carrying the two-point correlation and a local
remainder,

$$
F[\psi] \;=\; \int \Big[ \tfrac12\,\psi\,\big(C(\nabla^2)\big)\,\psi
                        \;+\; f_{\mathrm{loc}}(\psi,\psi_{\mathrm{MF}}) \Big]\,
          d\mathbf{x}.
$$ {#eq-w-energy}

The local part is a polynomial in $\psi$ and in a mean-field-filtered density
$\psi_{\mathrm{MF}}$, with coefficients $p_2,p_3,p_4$ and $q_{20},\dots,q_{40}$
that encode the solid and vapour branches of the equation of state.

## Spectral formulation

Writing $u = k_{\mathrm{lap}} = -|\mathbf{k}|^2$ as in @sec-klap, the
evolution operator is

$$
L(k) \;=\; u\;C(k), \qquad M_{\mathrm{nl}}(k) \;=\; u ,
$$ {#eq-w-symbol}

so both the linear and the nonlinear channel carry the conserving factor $u$.

The correlation symbol $C(k)$ is built around a peak at $|\mathbf{k}|=1$, which
is what selects the lattice constant. With $\kappa = |\mathbf{k}|-1$ measuring
distance from the peak,

$$
C(k) \;=\; \underbrace{P_{\mathrm{stab}}}_{\text{ETD stabiliser}}
        \;+\; \bar p_2
        \;-\; \underbrace{B_x\,e^{-T/T_0}\,g(\kappa)}_{\text{correlation peak}}
        \;+\; \bar q_2\, f_{\mathrm{MF}}(k),
$$ {#eq-w-ck}

with a deliberately **asymmetric** peak shape

$$
g(\kappa) \;=\;
\begin{cases}
  \exp\!\big(-\kappa^2/\alpha^2\big), & \kappa < 0 \quad\text{(Gaussian side)},\\[4pt]
  1 - \kappa^2/\alpha^2,              & \kappa \ge 0 \quad\text{(parabolic side)},
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-w-peak}

@eq-w-peak is the $\alpha_{\mathrm{highOrd}} = 0$ form. Every shipped preset
sets $\alpha_{\mathrm{highOrd}} = 4$, which adds a higher-order term
$r_{\mathrm{tol}}\,\kappa^{4}$ inside the Gaussian exponent, with
$r_{\mathrm{tol}}$ fixed by the far-field tolerance `alpha_farTol`. The effect
is to pull the Gaussian side down faster far from the peak; the shape near
$\kappa = 0$ is unchanged.

and a mean-field filter

$$
f_{\mathrm{MF}}(k) \;=\; e^{\,u/\lambda^2}.
$$ {#eq-w-mf}

Two details in @eq-w-ck matter for the numerics rather than the physics. The
$e^{-T/T_0}$ factor makes the peak depth temperature-dependent, which is how
melting enters. The $P_{\mathrm{stab}}$ term is a constant shift added to
$C$ and subtracted again inside the pointwise nonlinearity; it moves $L$ away
from zero for the modes that would otherwise sit near the stability boundary,
which is what lets ETD take a useful timestep. It changes the split, not the
solution.

An optional thermal drive $G_{\mathrm{grid}}$, $V_{\mathrm{grid}}$ imposes a
moving temperature gradient for directional-solidification studies. When
omitted the run is isothermal.

## Solution strategy

ETD1 as in @eq-etd1, with one $\psi$ field and a filtered
$\psi_{\mathrm{MF}}$ derived from it each step. Two transforms per step.

Unlike the high-order spectral chapters that follow, **this application does
not dealias**: `SpectralETDOptions::dealias` defaults to `false` and neither
the tungsten session nor the JSON path ever turns it on. What that costs is
measured in @sec-tungsten-dealias below, and the answer is not the one the
sentence above invites — the flag cannot simply be switched on at the shipped
resolution.

For moving-front studies the application supports a `moving` boundary
condition that tracks the solidification front along $x$ and shifts the
computational window to follow it. The tracked front state — the unwrapped
position, the scan index, and a first-detection flag — is part of the
checkpoint, so a restarted two-leg run continues the same interface rather than
re-detecting it at $t=0$.

## Resolution and the dealiasing question {#sec-tungsten-dealias}

The nonlinearity is cubic, $\bar p_3\psi^2+\bar p_4\psi^3$, and the
correlation kernel is a function of $|k|-1$, so the crystal sits at
$k_0=1$ and carries genuine content at $2k_0$ and $3k_0$. Whether a grid can
represent that honestly turns on two conditions, both set by
$k_{\mathrm{Ny}}=\pi/\Delta x$:

1. the third harmonic must fit under Nyquist, $3k_0\le k_{\mathrm{Ny}}$,
   or it folds back onto a resolved mode;
2. the 2/3 dealiasing cut must clear the second harmonic,
   $2k_0\le\frac{2}{3}k_{\mathrm{Ny}}$, or switching the mask on deletes part
   of the crystal itself.

Both reduce to $\Delta x\le\pi/3$, six grid points per lattice period. **Every
shipped preset uses $\Delta x=1.1107$, which is 6.1% coarser than that**, and
therefore fails both at once: with the mask off the third harmonic aliases from
$3.0$ back onto $k=2.657$; with it on, the cut at $1.886$ sits below the
crystal's own second harmonic at $2.0$. There is no good side to the
comparison at this spacing — which is why the honest fix is resolution, not
the flag.

`tungsten_dealias_study` measures it: the same seeded solidification, the same
initial condition, the same 1000 steps, run twice at each spacing with the mask
off and on.

| points / period | $\Delta x$ | $3k_0$ resolved | mask spares $2k_0$ | $\Delta$ power | $\Delta\max\psi$ | $\Delta k_1$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.66 (**shipped**) | 1.1107 | no | no | 1.70 % | 1.07 % | 9e-06 |
| 6.00 | 1.0472 | yes | yes | 1.27 % | 1.04 % | 1.4e-04 |
| 6.67 | 0.9425 | yes | yes | 0.48 % | 0.29 % | 4.7e-04 |
| 8.00 | 0.7854 | yes | yes | **0.009 %** | 0.018 % | 2.5e-06 |

![What the 2/3 dealias mask changes in a tungsten solidification, against grid
resolution. Below six points per lattice period the grid cannot represent the
crystal's own harmonics, so neither mask setting is right; by eight points the
two agree to one part in $10^4$. The $k_1$ curve is not a
trend — see the text.](figures/tungsten_dealias_resolution.svg){#fig-tungsten-dealias}

Reading that across:

* **At the shipped resolution the choice is worth about 2%** in total spectral
  power and 1% in peak density. That is not nothing, and nothing in the
  repository currently states it.
* **It is a discretisation artefact, not a modelling choice.** Going from 5.66
  to 8 points per period collapses the discrepancy by a factor of 190, to
  0.009%. At adequate resolution the mask has nothing to remove and nothing to
  repair, which is exactly what an aliasing artefact should do.
* **The headline observable is robust.** The selected wavenumber $k_1$ — the
  lattice constant, which is what a PFC run is usually read for — differs by at
  most $5\times10^{-4}$ relative at any resolution, two to three orders below
  the power and amplitude differences. Its variation across the table is
  non-monotone and shows no trend: at these magnitudes it is scatter between
  two nearly identical runs, not a resolution effect. Existing tungsten results
  are not in question on this point.

What the results published here therefore carry is a **$\sim$2% discretisation
uncertainty on amplitudes and spectral power**, and no meaningful uncertainty
on the selected wavenumber. Moving the presets to $\Delta x\le\pi/4$ would
remove it at 2.8$\times$ the cost per step in 3-D; that trade has not been
made here, but it is now a decision with numbers attached rather than an
inherited default.

Exact dealiasing of a *cubic* term is the 1/2 rule, $2k_0\le\frac12
k_{\mathrm{Ny}}$, i.e. eight points per period — the same spacing at which the
measured difference disappears. `tungsten/resolution.hpp` holds these criteria
as testable predicates rather than prose, and `[resolution]` pins them.

## Verification

* **Split-run equivalence.** A checkpoint-and-restart run reproduces an
  uninterrupted run: local fields agree within $10^{-12}$ and the saved front
  state agrees exactly, on one and two MPI ranks
  (`tungsten-moving-restart-2rank`).
* **Golden regression.** One CPU checksum is pinned to a literal
  (`tungsten-cpu-golden`: a 32³, 10-step sine-initial-condition case). The
  4-rank test (`tungsten-golden-4rank`) checks only that the global checksum is
  finite and positive — it is a crash guard, not a pinned value.
* **CPU/GPU agreement.** `SPECTRAL_CHECKSUM` from 1 GCD and 16 GCDs agrees to
  about $10^{-12}$ relative. This figure comes from LUMI-G job records quoted
  in @sec-scalability, not from a committed artefact: the performance baselines
  in the repository store timings only, so the number cannot be re-checked from
  a clone.
* **Fail-closed restart.** A checkpoint missing front state, or one whose
  boundary configuration has changed, is a startup error rather than a silent
  re-detection.

There is no closed-form solution to compare against here — that is the price of
a realistic equation of state — so the coverage is regression and
self-consistency rather than analytical. The high-order spectral chapters that
follow are the ones carrying analytical checks.

## Binaries and inputs

`tungsten` (CPU), `tungsten_cuda`, `tungsten_hip`. Inputs under
`inputs_json/` and `inputs_toml/`: single seed, fixed and moving boundary
conditions, restart, and a performance configuration.

## Scalability

Measured on LUMI-G from 1 to 32 GCDs at $768^3$; see @sec-scalability. This is
the model used for the sizing sweep that fixes the single-GCD working point.
